title: miR-206 orchestrates breast cancer radiosensitivity through a SIRT1/p53 feedback loop: a network medicine modelling study.
authors: Fontinele, Djorkaeff O; Reiniger, Klaus A R; Azevedo, Arthur H D; Lima, Joao Paulo M S; Gupta, Shantanu
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过网络医学建模分析miR-206/SIRT1/p53调控回路与乳腺癌放疗敏感性，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且方法为网络建模而非AI/物理模拟，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy remains a cornerstone of breast cancer treatment, yet radioresistance limits its efficacy. miR-206 acts as a tumor suppressor by inhibiting SIRT1 and stabilizing p53. However, how these molecular components are organized within larger regulatory networks, and whether such network-level hubs can be therapeutically prioritized, remains unclear. RESULTS: Network modeling predicted a previously unrecognized double-negative feedback loop (miR-206  dash, vertical SIRT1  dash, vertical p53 --> miR-206) that functions as a predicted bistable switch, driving mutually exclusive commitment to either a radiosensitive (apoptotic) or a radioresistant (proliferative) fate. Monte Carlo simulations revealed that opposite perturbations of this circuit consistently drove the system toward the corresponding stable attractor. Edge disruption analysis identified the miR-206/SIRT1 and p53/miR-206 interactions as essential for maintaining bistability, while ATM exerted p53-dependent context-specific effects. Model predictions were consistent with independent experimental observations that miR-206 overexpression suppresses SIRT1, enhances p53 acetylation, and increases radiosensitivity. CONCLUSIONS: This network medicine framework identifies the miR-206/SIRT1/p53 bistable switch as a key regulatory module governing cell-fate decisions in breast cancer radioresistance. The model provides a systems-level platform for prioritizing experimentally testable therapeutic strategies to overcome radioresistance.
abstract_zh: 背景：放射治疗仍是乳腺癌治疗的基石，但放射抗性限制了其疗效。miR-206通过抑制SIRT1并稳定p53发挥肿瘤抑制因子的作用。然而，这些分子组分如何在更大的调控网络中被组织，以及此类网络级枢纽是否可被治疗性地优先靶向，仍不清楚。结果：网络建模预测了一个先前未被识别的双负反馈回路（miR-206 减号、竖线 SIRT1 减号、竖线 p53 --> miR-206），该回路作为一个预测的双稳态开关，驱动细胞向放射敏感（凋亡）或放射抗性（增殖）命运进行互斥性承诺。蒙特卡洛模拟显示，对该回路的相反扰动持续将系统推向相应的稳定吸引子。边缘破坏分析识别出miR-206/SIRT1和p53/miR-206相互作用为维持双稳态所必需，而ATM则发挥p53依赖的上下文特异性效应。模型预测与独立实验观察一致，即miR-206过表达抑制SIRT1、增强p53乙酰化并增加放射敏感性。结论：该网络医学框架将miR-206/SIRT1/p53双稳态开关识别为调控乳腺癌放射抗性中细胞命运决定的关键调控模块。该模型提供了一个系统级平台，用于优先排序可实验验证的克服放射抗性的治疗策略。
